subject.title: Remote skill bin probe times out when node is co-located with gateway (macOS app as node on same host)

question: For macOS app-backed nodes, should OpenClaw preserve advertised `system.which`/`system.run` and make remote skill-bin probing readiness-aware, or should it skip probes for co-located app nodes?
rationale: The choice changes remote exec compatibility, startup noise, stale-bin behavior, and skill availability freshness; source evidence shows the remaining timing risk but does not settle the product contract.

options.title: Defer And Back Off Probes
options.body: Preserve the macOS app command surface, delay the initial probe until the node is ready, add bounded retry/backoff, and require live co-located plus remote macOS proof.

options.title: Skip Co-Located App Probes Only
options.body: Suppress the same-host warning path while leaving remote macOS app probe timing to a separate follow-up.

options.title: Add Operator Disable Config
options.body: Add a suppression knob, accepting new config surface while leaving the default readiness behavior unresolved.

recommendation.title: Defer And Back Off Probes
recommendation.body: Preserve the macOS app command surface, delay the initial probe until the node is ready, add bounded retry/backoff, and require live co-located plus remote macOS proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest feature-history signal across remote skills, macOS node exec, and the security/product boundary affected by this choice.
